content.comment_body: When output Q1 switches off, I need to generate a pulse for the wiping relay to initiate the next step in the program. I tried using a wiping relay with the input inverted, but this activates during power-up, which is not desired. Any suggestions?
You could try using flag M8, it might help.

Connect the output Q1 to a NAND (Edge) block to create a pulse when Q1 turns off. From there, link to a latching relay (RS Relay) and then to the wiping relay. Don't forget to reset the RS block. Refer to the attachment for more details.
This works perfectly, thanks a lot.

analysis.insight_summary: The main challenge is sending a pulse to a wiping relay only when output Q1 turns off, without triggering it during system start-up. Current approaches cause unwanted activation at power-up, so users proposed using internal flags and function blocks for precise pulse generation. Implementing these suggestions solved the issue, resulting in positive feedback.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants a reliable method to pulse the wiping relay strictly when Q1 switches off, avoiding activation during system start-up.
